claims.text: The 19 June 1990 report records the police account of the offence: that Lazar recruited a prostitute, operated her business from the Newport Cove apartments, maintained computer records of customers and their licence plate numbers, and took at least half her earnings. It records the sentencing exposure as 'one to six years, with a possible fine of $5,000'. It also records, from police records, that 'Lazar told her he had master's degrees from two universities', which is the same credential claim appearing in a police file rather than a broadcast.

claims.text: CONTEMPORANEOUS CONFIRMATION OF THE 1989 REPORTING. A Las Vegas Review-Journal report of 19 June 1990, page 8B, by Warren Bates, records that 'Lazar was the focal point for much of KLAS-TV, Channel 8 reporter George Knapp's award winning series'. This is the only contemporaneous documentary confirmation opened by this session that the 1989 Lazar broadcasts happened at all.

claims.text: KLAS-TV is the originating institution of the Bob Lazar claim. A Las Vegas Review-Journal report of 19 June 1990 records contemporaneously that Lazar 'was the focal point for much of KLAS-TV, Channel 8 reporter George Knapp's award winning series'. The station's own retrospectives on the story, at 8newsnow.com, returned HTTP 403 to three separate requests on 18 September 2026, so not one word of the originating institution's own account of its 1989 reporting is currently on this board.

claims.text: THE ANCHOR. A Las Vegas Review-Journal report of Tuesday 19 June 1990, page 8B, by Warren Bates, records contemporaneously that 'Lazar was the focal point for much of KLAS-TV, Channel 8 reporter George Knapp's award winning series'. This establishes that the 1989 broadcasts existed, that Lazar was their centre, and that they had already won recognition by mid-1990.
